req.title: Basic-auth handles special characters
req.statement: The system shall URL-decode <user> and <passwd> path segments before comparing against the supplied Basic credentials.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> must URL-decode path segments before comparing against Basic credentials. I need to test: (1) positive case with URL-encoded special chars in path that match decoded credentials, (2) negative case where credentials don't match after decoding, (3) boundary case with minimally encoded chars (e.g., space as %20), (4) decision table covering both user and passwd encoding, (5) negative path where wrong decoded value is supplied. The check_basic_auth function compares auth.username == user and auth.password == passwd, so the route handler receives the decoded path segments from Flask/Werkzeug and compares them directly. I must assert exact status codes (200 vs 401) and exact JSON payload fields to kill comparison-mutation and constant-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_basic_auth_url_encoded_special_chars_positive
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Client sends Basic credentials matching URL-decoded path segments
actions: URL-encode special characters in user and passwd path segments
Send GET /basic-auth/<encoded_user>/<encoded_passwd> with matching Basic auth header
expected: JSON body contains authenticated=true and user equal to decoded username
trace: R-HTTPBIN-041: system shall URL-decode path segments before comparing
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

user = 'user@example'
passwd = 'p@ss!word'
encoded_user = 'user%40example'
encoded_passwd = 'p%40ss%21word'

credentials = base64.b64encode(f'{user}:{passwd}'.encode()).decode()
headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {credentials}'}

def test_basic_auth_url_encoded_special_chars_positive():
    r = client.get(f'/basic-auth/{encoded_user}/{encoded_passwd}', headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data['authenticated'] == True
    assert data['user'] == user

tests.name: test_basic_auth_no_credentials_returns_401
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send GET /basic-auth/user/passwd with no Authorization header
trace: R-HTTPBIN-041: missing credentials must yield 401 (check_basic_auth returns falsy when auth is None)
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

def test_basic_auth_no_credentials_returns_401():
    r = client.get('/basic-auth/user/passwd')
    assert r.status_code == 401
    assert 'WWW-Authenticate' in r.headers
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is None or 'authenticated' not in (data or {})

tests.name: test_basic_auth_encoded_at_sign_user_mismatch_decision_table
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
User sends literal encoded string as credentials instead of decoded value
actions: Path has %40 for @; client sends literal 'user%40example' as username (not decoded)
This tests that comparison is against decoded value, not raw encoded string
expected: HTTP 401 response because credentials contain literal %40 not @
trace: R-HTTPBIN-041: comparison must be against decoded path, so literal %40 != @
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

encoded_user = 'user%40example'
encoded_passwd = 'p%40ss'

literal_user = 'user%40example'
literal_passwd = 'p%40ss'
credentials = base64.b64encode(f'{literal_user}:{literal_passwd}'.encode()).decode()
headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {credentials}'}

def test_basic_auth_encoded_at_sign_user_mismatch_decision_table():
    r = client.get(f'/basic-auth/{encoded_user}/{encoded_passwd}', headers=headers)
    assert r.status_code == 401
